o.text:
Morphologically çox (“much, many”) + -luq.
The sense 'set' is a semantic loan from Russian мно́жество (mnóžestvo).

Derived from Proto-Common Turkic *külgü. By surface analysis, gül- + -gü.
Cognates
* Kazakh күлкі (külki, “laugh, mockery”),
* Bashkir көлкө (külkü, “laughter; laughing stock”),
* Uzbek kulgi (“laughter”),
* Kyrgyz күлкү (külkü, “laughter”),
* Tatar көлке (kölke, “laughter”),
* Uyghur كۈلكە (külke, “laughter”),
* Karachay-Balkar кюлкю (külkü, “laughter”),
* Kumyk кюлкю (külkü, “laughter”),
* Nogai куьлки (külki, “laughter”),
* Turkmen gülki (“laughter”),
* Krymchak кӱлькы (“laughter”),
* Crimean Tatar külkü (“laughter”), külgü (“laughter”),
* Karakalpak kúlki (“laughter”),
* Southern Altai кӱлкӱ (külkü, “laughter”)
